inputs.original_text: The “No Kings” rally against Trump shows what happens when political theatrics are allowed to crowd out respect for the law. Streets are not a stage for agitators to confront authorities, and slogans do not excuse disorder. Federal officers used tear gas and made arrests; at least 13 were confirmed in Portland and Denver. A decent society depends on clear rules and the courage to enforce them—not on treating chaos as ordinary political expression.
inputs.modified_text: The “No Kings” rally is a reminder that political protest does not put anyone above the law. When activists turn public streets into a stage for confrontation, the result is disorder—not some noble substitute for civic responsibility. Federal officers used tear gas and made arrests, with at least 13 confirmed in Portland and Denver. A country cannot function if every crowd decides its own rules; leaders should defend public order, and citizens should stop mistaking defiance for virtue.
